messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace procurement & purchase path — follow-up and intake

Hi Megan — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single place to track next steps and procurement asks.

Call highlights (short):
- Solstice is evaluating Redwood primarily for inference on clinical NLP workloads (gen/embeddings) with an initial pilot for 3 months.
- Preference: prefer vendor invoices / Net-30 PO. Finance typically issues POs via their procurement portal.
- Marketplace interest: technical/finance teams are open to AWS Marketplace if it simplifies procurement, but they need to confirm whether Private Offer (PO via marketplace) is supported and how invoicing works. GCP/Azure not in scope for pilot but could be later.
- Compliance: SOC 2 attestation and US data residency are hard requirements for pilot.

Immediate asks for procurement team (from today's call):
1) Can Redwood accept a PO (Net-30) — either directly or via AWS Private Offer?
2) If we go via AWS Marketplace, what does the invoice flow look like (billing to Solstice vs. vendor direct)? Timing of invoice generation and payment terms?
3) Example pricing SKUs / a short pricing snapshot for a 3-month pilot (estimate for monthly consumption).
4) I'll share an intake checklist for your procurement folks to complete (attached).

Next steps I propose:
- Megan / procurement: review the attached intake checklist and drop answers back to this thread (or upload to the Drive link shared).
- Redwood: Karthik + Monica to confirm marketplace PO/private-offer flow and provide a pricing snapshot and standard PO template.
- Schedule a procurement call for detailed billing/legal questions if the checklist shows marketplace interest.

Attachments: solstice_intake_checklist.pdf (attached) — short form covering billing contact, tax/registration, preferred payment terms, and required contract clauses.

Planned timeline: hoping to align procurement/finance the week of July 5 so we can start pilot mid-July.

Thanks — let me know if anything above is missing or if you want me to loop in legal early.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the checklist. A few quick clarifications from procurement side: 

- We typically use POs (Net-30). Our procurement portal is used to manage vendor onboarding; vendor must accept PO terms.
- AWS Marketplace is fine if Redwood can support a Private Offer that allows us to apply a PO and Net-30 terms. If Marketplace invoice flow forces immediate payment by card or passthrough that doesn't map to our PO process, finance will flag it.
- Compliance: we require SOC 2 Type II and data residency in the US. Can you confirm those are available?
- Pricing: can you provide a short SKU-level estimate for a 3-month pilot (we expect ~60M tokens total) and indicate whether there are discounts for committed minimums?

I'll get procurement@solstice to begin the vendor intake once we have the checklist completed and some initial answers on marketplace/PO flow.

Thanks,
Megan Li
Director of Product Operations | Solstice Health
megan.li@solsticehealth.com

Hi team — quick answers / suggested next steps so we can respond to Solstice this afternoon: 

1) AWS Marketplace / Private Offer: Yes, Redwood supports AWS Marketplace Private Offers. We can create a Private Offer that maps to the customer account and allow them to submit a PO on their side. In that flow AWS will record the purchase but Redwood invoices the customer directly under Net-30 if we opt into direct invoicing. (If we elect AWS-managed billing, the payment collection timing depends on AWS terms; prefer direct invoicing for Net-30 customers.)

2) Invoicing flow: For Solstice (Net-30 PO) we recommend provisioning a Private Offer and electing vendor-direct invoicing so Redwood issues invoices Net-30 to Solstice and Finance records payment when it arrives. This avoids forcing a credit-card payment flow.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is available. We also have options for US-only data residency under Redwood Private / VPC configurations; for pilot we can commit to regional hosting in us-west-2 and provide the SOC 2 report.

4) Pricing snapshot: attaching a short SKU-level estimate for a 3-month pilot (assumes ~60M tokens): redwood_marketplace_pricing_snapshot.xlsx (attached). Summary: estimated monthly spend ~$2,400 (with standard PLG credits applied) — include a 10% committed usage discount for a 3-month pilot if Solstice signs a pilot MSA. Exact numbers depend on chosen model sizing and quantization profile.

5) Next internal steps:
- Monica: prepare the short PO template and vendor-terms summary for procurement.
- Vanessa: send the Private Offer approach + pricing snapshot back to Solstice and propose a 30-minute procurement call (include AWS-specific billing contact).
- I'll prepare the SOC2 extract and link to the compliance pack.

Procurement call suggestion: Fri Jul 2, 2026 — 10:00 AM PT (I'll block tentative on the calendar; Vanessa, can you confirm availability with Solstice?)

If we want, I can also draft the minimal statement to attach to the intake checklist about the invoice flow (one paragraph explaining vendor-direct invoicing on Private Offer).

Thanks — Karthik
